elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Inserted Ownership clause: "The Company shall own all right, title and interest in the Site, the Content and all other deliverables and work product created for the Company under this Agreement" — direct vesting in the Customer (the Company).

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Same sentence: "and HDI hereby assigns the same to the Company" — present-tense assignment by the Vendor of the Site, Content and all other deliverables/work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "HDI retains all right, title and interest in its pre-existing intellectual property" — express carve-out preserving Vendor's prior IP, consistent with the playbook (Vendor keeping its platform is acceptable).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "hereby grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to any such HDI intellectual property embedded in the Site or other deliverables" — "perpetual" is present.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same grant expressly states "irrevocable"; the licence is untied to termination or continued payment.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Same grant expressly states "royalty-free"; no additional fee, uplift or true-up is imposed elsewhere in the inserted text.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: "The Company retains all right, title and interest in all user, customer and transaction data collected through the Site"; Company-supplied Content is separately owned under the first sentence, and §8.1 continues to treat user information and data as the Company's Confidential Information. Scope is limited to data "collected through the Site", but that matches the data this Agreement generates.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "No intellectual property shall be owned jointly by the Parties." — express exclusion of joint ownership; no other provision (§§1.2, 5.2, 5.3, 6.1, 8.1) creates shared title.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: The insertion assigns "all other deliverables and work product created for the Company" and reserves to HDI only "its pre-existing intellectual property"; there is no carve-out for generic tools, methodologies or know-how developed during the engagement. To complete the fallback the drafter would need to add words such as "HDI retains ownership of its generic tools, methods and know-how, whether pre-existing or developed in the course of the Services".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise as drafted: the Company takes outright ownership of the Site, Content and other deliverables by assignment, which is a strictly greater and unlimited-in-time right than a perpetual licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No licence is needed because title vests in the Company by assignment; ownership cannot be revoked by HDI and no termination or clawback trigger is attached in the inserted text.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The assignment of "all right, title and interest" is territorially unqualified, so the Company's rights are at least worldwide in scope.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Ownership passes with no royalty, licence fee or usage charge; the only fee mechanics elsewhere (§1.2 places development, hosting and operating costs on HDI) are unaffected.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: As owner the Company may use and modify without restriction; this is reinforced by existing §5.2 giving the Company "exclusive artistic and editorial control over the Site".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Ownership carries the right to license and sublicense; nothing in the inserted clause or the surviving text restricts the Company's ability to grant rights in the Site or deliverables.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single inserted Ownership section supplies every preferred element in operative language — Company ownership of the Site/Content/deliverables, a present-tense HDI assignment, HDI's pre-existing IP carve-out, a perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence to embedded HDI IP, Company retention of user, customer and transaction data, and an express bar on joint ownership. Nothing is left only in the margin comment.

The fallback checklist is not independently complete (no reservation of HDI's generic tools and know-how developed during the engagement), but that element protects the Vendor and is immaterial because the preferred level is fully met; if the fallback is ever traded to, add an express carve-out for HDI's generic tools, methods and know-how.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion for a genuinely missing clause, no deletions, and the favourable existing provisions survive untouched — §5.2 editorial control and written acceptance, §5.3 merchant-of-record and title to Deerskin Products, §6.1 the narrow Marks licence to HDI with the no-implied-licence backstop, and §8.1 confidentiality over Content, user information and data. No operative term is duplicated and no requirement outside the IP checklist (indemnity, escrow, audit) is bolted on.

Intent preserved: the clause allocates only intangible rights and does not disturb §1.2 (HDI bears development and hosting costs), §5.3 (title to physical Deerskin Products) or the General Manager/day-to-day operating mechanics; the deterministic check confirms no residual assignment of Company IP or data to HDI.

Optional, non-blocking polish for the next turn: the data sentence is limited to data "collected through the Site" — consider "all Content, user, customer and transaction data provided by or collected for the Company" so Company data given to HDI outside the Site is caught; and, to avoid HDI arguing it lacks rights to perform, you may add "HDI may use the foregoing solely to perform its obligations under this Agreement", which costs us nothing given §1.1.
